Article Title: Virginia paid $29,700 for a temporary 1,458-square-foot easement behind a couple's home; their expert claimed a highway expansion caused almost $500,000 in losses, but an appeals court rejected that c
Article Text:
Virginia appeals court rejected couple’s claim for additional compensation over highway expansion (AI image)

Dispute began over a small strip of land

Lower court blocks wider project damages

Appeals court explains why additional damages were rejected

A Virginia couple who wanted additional compensation for the impact of a highway expansion on their property have lost their legal battle. An appeals court has ruled that they cannot claim losses caused by the wider road project when the government had temporarily acquired only a small section of their land.According to Find Law, Omar Mohammad El-Rashed and Eliana Eyad Albelbaisi owned a home in McLean, Virginia, near Interstate 495 (I-495). In March 2023, the Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) began proceedings to use a portion of their property temporarily for construction work.The land involved was a narrow strip at the back of their home, covering 1,458 square feet. VDOT offered $29,700 for its temporary use, including compensation for trees and vines. The couple accepted the payment but continued to argue that the amount did not cover the financial impact of the project on their property.Their appraiser, Dennis Gruelle, estimated that the highway expansion and the temporary acquisition together could reduce the property's value by almost $500,000. The couple wanted this estimate considered while determining their compensation.However, the Court of Appeals of Virginia upheld the lower court's decision to exclude the larger damages claim.In its November 10 ruling, the court said the compensation had to relate to the land actually acquired and the effects directly caused by its temporary use. It also rejected the couple's request for legal fees and costs.Before the expansion, the section of I-495 near the couple's home had eight lanes. A sound wall and a wooded area stood between the highway and their property. VDOT owned land next to the couple's parcel, with trees on both sides of the boundary.The department sought temporary rights over a strip less than 10 feet wide behind the house. The 1,458-square-foot area was required for construction activities involving slopes. VDOT valued its use at $29,700, of which $28,200 was for the temporary construction easement and $1,500 covered natural trees and vines.The couple believed the offer was insufficient. They initially argued that the land's rental value over an estimated five-year period was $50,495. They also placed the value of the landscaping taken by VDOT at $3,000, bringing their estimate for the easement itself to $53,495.Their appraiser also considered the possible impact on the entire residential property. He attributed the estimated reduction of almost $500,000 to the removal of trees, the rebuilding of the sound wall closer to the house and the new highway lanes being closer to the property.The Commissioner of Highways opposed this larger estimate. The department argued that the couple could seek compensation for the temporary acquisition, but could not include losses arising from the entire I-495 expansion.The dispute went before a circuit court, where the Commissioner asked the judge to prevent Gruelle from presenting his nearly $500,000 estimate.The department's position was that the government had acquired only a temporary right to use a small portion of the property. The wider highway construction was a separate matter, and the claimed reduction in the home's value was not directly linked to the land acquired.The circuit court accepted this argument. It allowed evidence about losses connected to the temporary easement but excluded the appraiser's assessment of the wider project's impact.The court also ruled that the couple could not seek compensation for effects such as noise, dust, vibration and the loss of trees from land already owned by VDOT when those effects were linked to the larger construction project.Following this decision, the couple obtained another assessment from Gruelle. He calculated that disruption directly associated with the temporary easement, including noise, dust, vibration and the use of other parts of their property to reach the construction area, could reduce the remaining property's value by $124,850, or five per cent.However, the department also challenged this revised estimate. Before the circuit court ruled on that challenge, both sides reached an agreement. They fixed compensation for the temporary easement at $29,700, while allowing the couple to appeal the earlier decision excluding their wider damages claim.The couple argued that compensation should account for the full I-495 project rather than just the temporary use of their land. They relied on Virginia's rules for calculating the value of acquired property and damage to the land that remains with its owner.The appeals court disagreed. It said the central issue was the connection between the government's acquisition and the losses claimed by the couple.Under Virginia law, compensation can cover damage to the remaining property when that damage results from the acquisition. But the judges found that the couple's larger claim arose mainly from the highway expansion, not from the temporary easement itself.The court also examined whether the claimed effects were specific to the couple's property. It found that the wider project's impact, including construction noise and changes affecting nearby properties, could also be experienced by other landowners in the area.The judges distinguished these effects from disruption caused directly by VDOT's temporary use of the acquired strip. They said the couple had already received compensation for losses associated with that temporary use under their agreement.The ruling did not mean that every form of damage to the remaining property was excluded. The court noted that direct physical damage caused by the department's use of the acquired land, such as damage to the house or landscaping, could qualify for compensation.However, the couple's appeal concerned losses attributed to the highway project as a whole. The court found that these did not meet the legal requirements for additional compensation in this case.El-Rashed and Albelbaisi also asked the appeals court to reimburse the legal expenses they had incurred while pursuing higher compensation.The judges rejected this request because the couple had not established a contractual, statutory or other legal basis for recovering those costs.

Article Title: Meet Jhon Jairo 'Popeye' Velásquez, Pablo Escobar's hitman who helped coordinate 3,000 killings before becoming a famous Colombian YouTuber recounting his days in the Medellín cartel
Article Text:
The boy who dreamed of joining the police

The life of a killer

A repentant man?

He helped coordinate 3,000 murders, served 23 years in prison and came back only to become one of Colombia 's most famous YouTubers. Jhon Jairo Velásquez was one of Pablo Escobar's deadliest hitmen. Nicknamed 'Popeye' his victims included prominent politicians, underworld rivals and even an airplane full of innocent civilians.During the 1980s and early 90s, Velásquez murdered more than 250 people and arranged 3,000 additional killings for Escobar and the Medellín Cartel. He was arrested in 1992 and spent nearly 23 years behind bars for murder, drug trafficking and terrorism, among other crimes. After his release in 2014, he began a career completely unexpected for a criminal, he became a YouTube star. He began a channel titled 'Repentant Popeye' and criticised the Colombian government while recounting some of his most infamous hits, according to a report by All That's Interesting.Jhon Jairo Velásquez was born in Yarumal, Colombia in 1962. He dropped out of high school to join the Colombian Navy, where he earned the nickname “Popeye” due to his appearance. However, he soon left and started training to become a police officer.When it didn't work out, a friend found 17-year-old Velasquez a job as a driver and bodyguard for a young woman, who also happened to be Pablo Escobar's girlfriend. By the time he was 18, Velásquez had received orders to carry out his first hit for the up-and-coming Medellín Cartel.“I had to kill a bus dispatcher,” Velásquez told Revista Bocas in a 2013 interview. “Back when the man was a driver, the mother of a friend of Pablo Escobar boarded his bus; he pulled away before she could get off, causing her to fall. He left her lying on the ground without offering any help, and she died.”When Escobar's friend asked him to seek revenge, Velásquez was assigned the task. “I handled reconnaissance, tracked the guy down, and killed him,” Velásquez recalled. “I didn’t feel a thing… I haven’t lost any sleep over the acts I’ve committed.”With his first kill under the belt, Velásquez soon gained the trust of Escobar and quickly rose through the ranks of the cartel.Over the next decade, he killed more than 250 people for Escobar. He took out journalists, drug trafficking rivals, high-profile political figures, and even his own girlfriend. Around 1984, Velásquez arranged the murder of Wendy Chavarriaga Gil, who had previously dated Escobar himself. Velásquez loved her, but Escobar believed she was working as an informant, so she had to die. “What happened with Wendy was madness,” Velásquez told Revista Bocas. “I sent a group of guys… who were under my command. I couldn’t bring myself to carry it out personally. I set up a meeting for her, and they took care of it.”In the 1980s, Velásquez was involved in Escobar's most notorious crimes. In January 1988, Velásquez helped orchestrate the kidnapping of Andrés Pastrana Arango, who was running for mayor of Bogotá. The police found him a week later, and he went on to become the president of Colombia in 1998. Just a week after Pastrana’s abduction, the cartel kidnapped Carlos Mauro Hoyos, another Colombian politician. There are several versions of the story, but according to Velásquez himself, he was ordered to assassinate Hoyos. While the Colombian Army was out searching for Hoyos, Velásquez reportedly disguised himself in a sweater and glasses and bypassed a military checkpoint by claiming to be a student delivering medicine to a relative. When he arrived at the ranch where Hoyos was being held, Velásquez shot him three times.The following year, he helped arrange the murder of presidential candidate Luis Carlos Galán, who was shot to death in front of 10,000 people while surrounded by 18 bodyguards as he walked onto a stage in Soacha to give a speech.However, his most famous crime came in November 1989, when he was involved in planning the bombing of Avianca Flight 203. The airplane left Bogotá with 101 passengers and six crew members — and an explosive planted inside. As the plane flew over Soacha, a young man pushed a button that he reportedly thought would record a conversation. Instead, it detonated the bomb, killing all 107 people on board and three more victims on the ground.Escobar targeted the plane because he thought that presidential candidate César Gaviria would be on the flight, but he was not, and he went on to win the 1990 election. By 1991, Escobar had arranged a deal to surrender to Colombian authorities if he could serve his sentence at La Catedral, the luxury prison he built for himself. Velásquez decided to go with him to serve as his bodyguard. And when Escobar eventually escaped and went on the run, Velásquez accompanied him.Finally, in October 1992, Jhon Jairo Velásquez turned himself in as the Medellín Cartel began to crumble. He was convicted of murder, terrorism, extortion, and drug trafficking, and he received the maximum sentence of 30 years. Velásquez was released in 2014, and began an unexpected new career as a YouTuber.Pablo Escobar died in a shootout with the police while Velásquez was behind bars, and Velásquez had decided not to return to his former life of crime. “I want to enjoy the little things in life now. One thing is certain: I will never again accept a contract to kill someone,” he told Revista Bocas a year before his release.Instead, Velásquez started a YouTube channel called “Repentant Popeye,” which gained more than 1.2 million followers. In his videos, he criticised Colombia’s government and recalled several of the murders he committed.Velásquez also helped produce a movie about his life and wrote two books: My Life as a Hitman for Pablo Escobar and Surviving Pablo Escobar: “Popeye” the Hitman.“I’m a professional killer; I killed for money,” Velásquez said in the 2017 documentary Escobar’s Hitman. “I also killed out of love and respect for Pablo Escobar.”As Velásquez told interviewers in 2013, “If Pablo Escobar were to be reborn, I would go with him without thinking.”Then, in 2018, Velásquez returned to prison for extortion and criminal conspiracy. Two years later, on Feb. 6, 2020, he died from oesophageal cancer at age 57.
Article Summary: Jhon Jairo Velásquez was one of Pablo Escobar's deadliest hitmen. Nicknamed 'Popeye' his victims included prominent politicians, underworld rivals and even an airplane full of innocent civilians. He was arrested in 1992 and spent nearly 23 years behind bars for murder, drug trafficking and terrorism, among other crimes. After his release in 2014, he became a YouTube star.

Article Title: Indian-origin trucker Ranjit Singh found guilty of smuggling 40kg cocaine worth $4.8m into Canada
Article Text:
Ranjit Singh/Image: Sarnia Observer

An Indian-origin truck driver has been convicted of importing cocaine worth up to $4.8 million into Canada after a judge rejected his explanation for how the drugs ended up inside his trailer during a border crossing in April 2024. Ranjit Singh , 33, was found guilty of importing cocaine and possessing it for trafficking on Monday after Ontario Superior Court Justice Scott Pratt ruled against him following a three-week trial in Sarnia in June.The case dates back to April 26, 2024, when Canadian authorities discovered 40 kilograms of cocaine packed inside two cardboard boxes in a truck at the Canadian side of the Blue Water Bridge. The drugs were estimated to be worth between $3.6 million and $4.8 million.“The defendant will be found guilty of both charges,” Pratt said while delivering his decision, which took approximately an hour.During the trial, prosecutors presented a sequence of events in which Singh allegedly collected packages of cocaine from another truck at a Pilot Travel Centre in Channahon, Illinois. The Crown further alleged that he purchased cardboard boxes from a Home Depot store in Shorewood, Illinois, before placing the drugs inside them.According to the prosecution's account, Singh subsequently loaded the packages onto his trailer at a truck yard on Sanders Road in Lansing, Michigan. The boxes were concealed within a pallet containing other goods before the vehicle travelled towards Canada.Singh disputed the prosecution's version of events. During several days of testimony, he acknowledged that cocaine had been discovered in his trailer but denied receiving or transporting the drugs knowingly.He told the court that the owner of his company had instructed him to purchase the cardboard boxes and leave them with another truck at the Michigan yard. Singh said he noticed an unidentified man at the location and left his vehicle unattended for between 10 and 15 minutes while he went to the bathroom.Justice Pratt rejected Singh's explanation, pointing to inconsistencies in his testimony. The judge said he was satisfied that Singh had probably received the cocaine from another driver at the Illinois travel centre, as the prosecution had argued.However, Pratt said the precise point at which Singh obtained the drugs was not decisive to the case. The cocaine was inside his trailer when he entered Canada, and the judge concluded that Singh knew it was there.Singh, who was granted bail of $200,000 in early May 2024, will remain out of custody until sentencing. A sentencing hearing has been scheduled for February, according to The London Free Press.
Article Summary: Ranjit Singh, 33, was found guilty of importing cocaine and possessing it for trafficking on Monday after Ontario Superior Court Justice Scott Pratt ruled against him. The case dates back to April 26, 2024, when Canadian authorities discovered 40 kilograms of cocaine packed inside two cardboard boxes in a truck at the Canadian side of the Blue Water Bridge.

Article Title: Yella Beezy found guilty of hiring gunman to kill rapper MO3
Article Text:
In a landmark ruling, Dallas rapper Yella Beezy has been handed a life sentence without parole for his orchestrating role in the capital murder of fellow rapper MO3, who was tragically shot in November 2020. (Pic Credit: AP)

Dallas rapper Yella Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, was convicted of capital murder by a Dallas County jury on Wednesday. He allegedly hired the gunman who killed fellow rapper MO3, born Melvin Noble.Beezy was sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, the Associated Press reported.“We don’t know what turned it for the jurors. We appreciate the verdict,” lead prosecutor Tommy Adams said. “We think they got it right today. It’s been one of the most challenging cases over the last six years.”According to the BBC, Beezy associate Kewon white was also convicted of capital murder and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Prosecutors identified White as the shooter who killed MO3 on a Dallas highway in November 2020.According to the prosecution, white pulled up alongside MO3’s vehicle on Interstate 35 in South Dallas, near the Dallas Zoo. He then chased the rapper on foot and fired more than 40 shots at him.
Article Summary: Dallas rapper Yella Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, was convicted of capital murder by a Dallas County jury on Wednesday. He allegedly hired the gunman who killed fellow rapper MO3, born Melvin Noble. Beezy was sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.

Article Title: In 2022, Puerto Rico put baseball legend Roberto Clemente's image on license plates without his sons' permission; after they sought $45 million in damages, the US Supreme Court declined their appeal
Article Text:
Photo: Roberto Clemente website

A tribute without permission

Roberto Clemente's image on license plates Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The legal argument

Why the courts sided with Puerto Rico

Clemente’s enduring legacy

What the decision means

The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to hear the appeal of Roberto Clemente’s sons, ending their effort to challenge Puerto Rico’s use of the baseball legend’s image on commemorative license plates. According to Reuters, USA Today and NewsNation, the justices rejected the case on November 9 without explanation, leaving in place lower-court rulings that favored Puerto Rico.The dispute began in 2022, when Puerto Rico issued special license plates and vehicle registration tags honoring Clemente on the 50th anniversary of his death. His sons said the territory used their father’s likeness without permission and sought $45 million in damages, along with $3.15 million for alleged trademark infringement. Read more details about this incident, as per the reports, here:Puerto Rico’s commemorative plates featured Clemente’s image, his No. 21 and a reference to his 3,000 career hits. The program was intended to mark 50 years since his death and celebrate one of Puerto Rico’s most beloved sports figures. But Clemente’s sons, Roberto Clemente Jr., Luis Roberto Clemente and Roberto Enrique Clemente, said they were never consulted. They argued that the territory appropriated a valuable family asset by using their father’s image without authorization.The license-plate program charged fees of $21 and $5, which raised a combined $15 million for Puerto Rico. The Clemente family said those revenues should have benefited their businesses, which they said protect the Roberto Clemente trademark, safeguard his legacy and promote his philanthropy.The family also objected to the timing. They argued that the fees were collected during a difficult economic period for Puerto Rico, while the island was recovering from bankruptcy, making the decision to charge residents for plates bearing Clemente’s image especially troubling.The sons filed suit in federal court in Puerto Rico, claiming that the government’s use of the trademark violated the Fifth Amendment’s prohibition on the taking of private property without just compensation. They asked the court to block future use of their father’s likeness on license plates and registration tags.Their argument centered on whether an intangible asset, such as a trademark or a person’s likeness, can be treated as property protected by the Fifth Amendment. The family’s lawyers said the lower courts wrongly suggested that the amendment does not automatically apply to intangible property in the same way it applies to land or other tangible assets.The Clemente family warned that the lower court’s reasoning could allow governments to take trademarks without paying for them, subject only to a balancing test that could leave owners with little protection. They argued that such a rule would invite governments to appropriate valuable intellectual property on demand.Puerto Rico disputed that interpretation. In its filing to the Supreme Court , the territory said the First Circuit did not categorically exclude intangible property from Fifth Amendment protection, but instead applied existing precedent to the specific facts of the case.A U.S. District Court judge in San Juan dismissed the case, finding that Puerto Rico was immune from the lawsuit. The First U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston later partially affirmed that dismissal, rejecting the family’s claim that Puerto Rico’s use of the trademark amounted to an unconstitutional taking.The appeals court also ruled that the Clemente family could not sue under the Fifth Amendment for intangible property such as a trademark. That conclusion was central to the case, because it meant the family could not pursue the damages they sought through that constitutional theory.Puerto Rico’s lawyers argued that the Supreme Court had no reason to intervene. They said the lower courts had followed established precedent and that there was no conflict among lower courts on the legal questions raised by the Clemente family.The Supreme Court agreed, declining to hear the case without comment. That decision does not create a new precedent, but it leaves the First Circuit’s ruling in place and closes the family’s path to a Supreme Court review in this dispute.Roberto Clemente remains one of baseball’s most admired figures, both for his performance on the field and for his humanitarian work. He played 18 seasons for the Pittsburgh Pirates from 1955 to 1972, earning 15 All-Star selections and winning two World Series titles.He was the World Series MVP in 1971 and finished his career with a .317 batting average, 3,000 hits, 1,305 RBIs and 240 home runs. The Baseball Hall of Fame inducted him posthumously in 1973, waiving its usual five-year waiting period.Clemente died at age 38 on December 31, 1972, in a plane crash while delivering humanitarian aid to earthquake victims in Nicaragua. His death transformed him into a symbol of service and sacrifice, and his legacy remains deeply meaningful in Puerto Rico and across baseball.The Supreme Court’s decision does not erase Clemente’s legacy or diminish the emotional weight of the dispute. It simply means that Puerto Rico will not face a federal constitutional trial over its use of the image on commemorative plates.For the Clemente family, the outcome is a legal setback, but it also highlights the ongoing challenge of protecting a loved one’s name and likeness after death. For Puerto Rico, it confirms that the state can honor a cultural icon through public programs without facing the constitutional claim the family pursued.The case may end in the courts, but the broader question it raised remains relevant. As governments increasingly use images, names and symbols to commemorate public figures, the line between a tribute and an unauthorized commercial use can become difficult to define.
Article Summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to hear the appeal of Roberto Clemente’s sons, ending their effort to challenge Puerto Rico's use of the baseball legend's image on commemorative license plates. The dispute began in 2022, when Puerto Rico issued special license plates and vehicle registration tags honoring Clemente on the 50th anniversary of his death. His sons sought $45 million in damages, along with $3.15 million for alleged trademark infringement.

Article Title: US closes a 4-kilometre road twice a year as thousands of snakes, including venomous rattlesnakes and cottonmouths, migrate between a swamp and limestone cliffs with changing temperatures
Article Text:
Image AI generated

Why do thousands of snakes migrate across Snake Road twice a year

US Forest Service enforces two seasonal road closures

Seasonal road closures protect snakes from deadly traffic

More than 23 snake species inhabit the Snake Road area

Visitors can explore Snake Road on foot during seasonal closures

A road in southern Illinois, United States, has an unusual reason for closing to traffic twice a year: thousands of snakes and other reptiles need to cross it during their seasonal migration. Known as Snake Road, the 4-kilometre stretch in Shawnee National Forest connects LaRue Swamp with the limestone cliffs of LaRue-Pine Hills. The animals travel towards the wetlands in spring to feed, mate and rest before returning to the cliffs in autumn for shelter. To protect them from passing vehicles, the US Forest Service closes the road during both migration periods, allowing visitors to explore it on foot.Snake Road lies between two important ecosystems in the Shawnee National Forest. To its west is LaRue Swamp, which forms part of the Mississippi River basin. To the east are the LaRue-Pine Hills, an area known for its limestone cliffs, which rise 46 metres above the surrounding landscape.The seasonal movement takes place as temperatures change. In spring, reptiles emerge from hibernation as the weather becomes warmer and travel towards the swamp, where they can feed, mate and rest. When autumn arrives and temperatures begin to fall, they return towards the limestone cliffs, which provide places to shelter from colder conditions.The US Forest Service closes Snake Road during two periods each year to protect migrating wildlife. According to the BBC, the road is closed from 15 March to 15 May in spring and from 1 September to 30 October in autumn.The closure dates were established following an earlier conservation measure introduced in 1972. Initially, the road was closed for three weeks during both the spring and autumn migration periods. However, biologist and herpetologist Scott Ballard, who worked with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources, found that the migration lasted longer than the original closure period. The Forest Service subsequently extended the restrictions to cover the longer migration.The seasonal closure is intended to prevent reptiles from being accidentally killed by traffic while crossing the road. Snakes and other cold-blooded animals can move particularly slowly during cooler periods, making it difficult for them to cross before vehicles approach.According to the BBC, the black asphalt can retain warmth during early mornings and evenings, but the reptiles may still move slowly. They also tend to stop when approached, including when a vehicle is coming towards them.The scale of the threat has also been documented in research. According to National Geographic, biologist Rich Siegel reported that almost one in four snakes he collected for a study had been killed by traffic. The seasonal road closure helps reduce this risk by removing vehicle traffic during the migration periods.More than 23 species of snakes have been recorded in the area, according to biologist Mark Vukovich, as reported by 5Chicago. The location is also home to several other reptiles and amphibians that use the route during their seasonal movements.Three of the snake species found in the area are venomous: the northern cottonmouth (Agkistrodon piscivorus), the copperhead (Agkistrodon contortrix) and the timber rattlesnake (Crotalus horridus). Other species that visitors may encounter include southern leopard frogs, different types of toads and salamanders, as well as turtles and lizards.These animals use the road as a passage between the two habitats. Their seasonal movement is the reason the Forest Service maintains restrictions on vehicles during specific months of the year.Although vehicles are prohibited during the seasonal closures, visitors are permitted to walk along the 4-kilometre stretch of Snake Road to observe the migrating wildlife. However, sightings are not necessarily as frequent as some visitors might expect.Scott Ballard explained that visitors should not expect to see large numbers of snakes crossing the road simultaneously. He said, "If you see twenty snakes while you're out here, that's a good day."Visitors are advised to observe the reptiles from a safe distance and avoid approaching, handling or startling them. Collecting reptiles is also prohibited under federal and state law.The seasonal closure allows snakes, amphibians and other reptiles to move between LaRue Swamp and the LaRue-Pine Hills without vehicle traffic during their migration. By restricting access to cars during these periods, the Forest Service protects wildlife travelling along one of the United States' most unusual roads.
Article Summary: Snake Road lies between two important ecosystems in Shawnee National Forest. In spring, reptiles emerge from hibernation and travel towards the swamp. When autumn arrives and temperatures begin to fall, they return towards the limestone cliffs of LaRue-Pine Hills. The US Forest Service closes Snake Road during two periods each year to protect migrating wildlife.

Article Title: Watch: US war secretary Pete Hegseth reprimanded by soldier at Arlington Cemetery
Article Text:
The incident occurred at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, one of the most revered war memorials in the US

Why Hegseth was reprimanded

Impeachment bid against Hegseth

US secretary of war Pete Hegseth was publicly reprimanded by a US Army soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery after members of his entourage were seen laughing and talking near the memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony.A video of the incident shows Hegseth posing for photographs with his wife, Jennifer, and senior members of his team on the steps in front of the tomb. As the group finished taking pictures, some members appeared to be laughing and chatting, prompting the soldier on duty to interrupt them and issue a reminder about the memorial's rules."All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the sentinel shouted, stopping his patrol and turning towards the group. The incident took place on Wednesday, a day after Hegseth narrowly survived an impeachment effort in the US House of Representatives.Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell defended the soldier's intervention, saying he had acted appropriately. "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Parnell said in a statement."The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored — and will always honor — the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe," he added.The incident occurred at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, one of the most revered war memorials in the US. It is the final resting place of unidentified American soldiers who died during World War I, World War II and the Korean War.The tomb has been guarded around the clock, regardless of weather conditions, by soldiers from the Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, known as 'The Old Guard', since 1948. Visitors are expected to maintain silence and show respect at the site.Hegseth and his entourage were visiting the cemetery as part of the Veterans Day commemorations, which were also attended by President Donald Trump and Vice-President JD Vance. The incident drew criticism from Democrats, with Representative Gwen Moore of Wisconsin accusing Hegseth of demonstrating "his utter lack of fitness for his office"."One day after narrowly avoiding impeachment, he shows his contempt for our men and women in uniform by disrespecting the sanctity of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier," she wrote in a social media post.The reprimand came a day after House Republicans blocked an attempt to impeach Hegseth, securing a procedural victory for the Trump administration.The effort was led by Republican Representative Thomas Massie, who introduced a resolution containing eight articles of impeachment. Hegseth was accused of authorising military operations in Iran and Yemen without congressional approval, violating the War Powers Act, and overseeing military actions involving civilian casualties and alleged extrajudicial killings.In a 211-204 vote on Tuesday, lawmakers agreed to refer the resolution to a committee, effectively preventing an immediate impeachment vote on the House floor.Hegseth dismissed the allegations during a Pentagon news conference, arguing that his actions did not amount to the "high crimes and misdemeanours" required for impeachment under the US Constitution. He described the effort as a political stunt and compared it to the unsuccessful impeachment attempts against Trump.However, the reprieve could be temporary. With Democrats set to take control of the House when the new Congress convenes in January, lawmakers could revive the impeachment effort.Trump has repeatedly backed Hegseth and praised his performance following the vote, awarding him an "A" PLUS PLUS PLUS on Truth Social while attacking Massie.
Article Summary: US secretary of war Pete Hegseth reprimanded by soldier guarding Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery. Members of his entourage were seen laughing and talking near the memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony. Incident took place on Wednesday, a day after he narrowly survived an impeachment effort in the US House of Representatives.

Article Title: Spain Protest: Protesters clash with police, set fires during Spain's general strike: Watch
Article Text:
Protesters set fires, clash with police during Spain's general strike: Watch

Poll Vote & Share your view Which factor do you think contributes most to the housing crisis in Spain? Rising rents Lack of affordable housing Government policies Speculation in the housing market 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Clashes broke out between masked protesters and police in Barcelona on Wednesday as tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike in 14 years, called by the country's major trade unions over the housing affordability crisis and rising cost of living.Around 120,000 people joined demonstrations in Madrid and more than 50,000 gathered in Barcelona, where some protesters set fire to rubbish bins, smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Officers fired tear gas to disperse the crowds, while transport and other public services across the country faced significant disruption.The disturbances in Barcelona continued into the evening, with a heavy police presence in the city centre. Some clashes took place along Passeig de Gràcia, near the iconic Plaça de Catalunya. Local media reported that protesters fired fireworks at police and looted shops, including a Lego store. Some were also seen attempting to enter an Apple Store.The unions said around four million workers participated in the nationwide strike, which was backed by Spain's two largest labour organisations, the UGT and CCOO, as well as tenants' associations protesting against rising rents and evictions.UGT chief Pepe Álvarez described the strike as a success, citing "massive" participation, while CCOO leader Unai Sordo said turnout was "very significant". However, participation varied across the country, with stronger support in coastal regions where housing pressures have been particularly acute.The walkout was the first general strike in Spain since 2012, when workers protested against austerity measures during the eurozone debt crisis. It comes less than three weeks before parliamentary elections scheduled for November 29.Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is seeking to make housing affordability a central election issue and shift the political debate away from corruption cases involving his inner circle and a deadly train crash last month. His Socialist Party, however, continues to trail in opinion polls.Spain faces a housing deficit of around 750,000 homes, which is projected to exceed one million by 2028, according to the country's central bank.With home ownership becoming increasingly unaffordable, demand for rental accommodation has risen sharply, putting further pressure on the market. The average monthly rent of 1,176 euros ($1,315) is equivalent to about 98.7 per cent of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.
Article Summary: Around 120,000 people joined demonstrations in Madrid and more than 50,000 gathered in Barcelona. Some protesters set fire to rubbish bins, smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Officers fired tear gas to disperse the crowds, while transport and other public services across the country faced significant disruption.

Article Title: Netanyahu asks military to prepare for Iran 2.0 as opposition demands no strikes before next govt
Article Text:
File photo: Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot (Photo: AP).

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 's security cabinet on Wednesday directed the military to prepare for a possible renewed attack on Iran, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot urged the caretaker government to avoid unnecessary military operations until a new administration takes office.“The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported.The security cabinet had last met on October 5, weeks before elections were held on October 27. The latest directives were publicised after Eisenkot called on Netanyahu to exercise restraint during the political transition.In a letter to Netanyahu, Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming Israel's next government, warned against launching military or security operations unless there was an immediate threat, Israeli media reported.According to the Ynet news website, Eisenkot said Netanyahu was leading a caretaker government that no longer enjoyed the confidence of the Knesset, Israel's parliament.“Only 46 Knesset members still support your continued tenure as prime minister,” he said.In a post shared on X, Eisenkot said Netanyahu had a responsibility to exercise particular caution while taking security and national decisions during the transition period.“The deployment of security forces without a direct and immediate threat that cannot be delayed could have devastating consequences for Israeli democracy and public trust in government institutions,” he warned.He urged Netanyahu to demonstrate restraint and avoid “dangerous moves” that could wait until a new government backed by the Knesset was sworn in.Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally tasked Eisenkot with forming the next government on Sunday after parliamentary factions representing 67 lawmakers recommended him. A total of 46 lawmakers backed Netanyahu, while seven declined to recommend either candidate, Anadolu Ajansi reported.Eisenkot has 28 days to form a governing coalition, with a possible 14-day extension.
Article Summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet directed the military to prepare for a possible renewed attack on Iran. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot urged the caretaker government to avoid unnecessary military operations until a new administration takes office. The security cabinet last met on October 5, weeks before elections were held on October 27.

Article Title: Trump administration aware of plans to oust Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Report
Article Text:
Trump administration aware of plans to oust Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Report

Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to discuss the future of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, with the Trump administration aware of plans to remove him from the position, a CBS News reporter said in a post on X.Meanwhile, Nvidia's board has been reportedly working with an external firm to identify potential successors to CEO Jensen Huang and is considering appointing an interim chief while searching for a permanent replacement, as per Bloomberg.Also Read| Nvidia shares fall 8% after hours as board reportedly weighs Jensen Huang's exit The reported developments follow revelations about two alleged extramarital relationships involving the 63-year-old executive, one of which involved a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence services.The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to meet as early as Thursday to discuss Huang's future at the company.The New York Times separately reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Citing five people who worked at the company, the newspaper said the relationship had not been previously reported.Also Read| Blacklisted Chinese military-linked university bought Nvidia H200 chips - Report According to the report, Huang and Powell, 48, were captured on video behaving affectionately at a hotel in San Jose, California, during an Nvidia conference in March.Powell joined Nvidia in 2008 and oversees programmes focused on applying the company's chip technology to higher education and healthcare, particularly medical imaging devices, according to Nvidia's website.The reported relationship has also raised questions about the company's workplace policies. Nvidia's code of conduct asks employees to "avoid situations where our actions create conflict", including "personal relationships". The company also states that it "promptly investigates reports of misconduct", The New York Times reported, noting that several corporations have policies restricting relationships between managers and their subordinates.Also Read| Nvidia Board issues another statement, two days after almost saying not 'firing' CEO Jensen Huang; says The latest revelations follow scrutiny of another reported relationship involving Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data company Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. US intelligence officials had identified her as an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.This was the relationship Huang acknowledged in a letter to Nvidia employees on Sunday. In the letter, he admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised for violating their trust.Following the acknowledgement, Nvidia's board reportedly launched an investigation into the matter, led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, according to The New York Times.The board was also considering Huang's position in light of the revelations involving both relationships, including the allegations concerning a possible connection to Chinese intelligence.Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has transformed the company into a leading supplier of artificial intelligence chips, becoming one of the most prominent figures in the global AI industry.
Article Summary: N Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to discuss the future of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. The Trump administration is aware of plans to remove him from the position, a CBS News reporter said. The reported developments follow revelations about two alleged extramarital relationships involving the 63-year-old executive. One of the relationships involved a businesswoman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence services.

Article Title: 10 killed as passenger vehicle plunges 500 metres down slope in Nepal
Article Text:
10 killed in passenger vehicle accident in Nepal (File photo)

At least 10 people were killed and five others injured on Thursday after a passenger vehicle plunged down a steep slope in Nepal's Makawanpur district in Bagmati province, according to media reports.The accident took place at around 5:45am when the vehicle, carrying around 15 people, was travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi, a local newspaper reported.The vehicle reportedly plunged around 500 metres down a steep slope, killing 10 people and injuring five others.The deceased included three women, two girls and five men, the report said, adding that their identities were yet to be established.The injured were taken to Hetauda Hospital for treatment, The Kathmandu Post reported.A seven-member rescue team was deployed to the accident site following reports of the crash, it added.
Article Summary: Vehicle plunged down a steep slope in Nepal's Makawanpur district. Accident took place at around 5:45am when the vehicle was travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi. The deceased included three women, two girls and five men, according to reports.

Article Title: ‘Mayday, mayday’: Bathroom leak floods Frontier flight, forces emergency landing in Chicago
Article Text:
Credit: Keegan Morris/Facebook

Video shows water flooding aircraft aisle

A leaking bathroom sink can be a nuisance at home. But when it happens thousands of feet in the air, with nowhere to escape the mess, it can quickly turn into an emergency. Passengers aboard a Frontier Airlines flight from Denver to Detroit experienced just that on Wednesday, when a burst bathroom faucet flooded the aircraft's cabin and forced the pilots to divert to Chicago.According to a post by The New York Post, Frontier Airlines Flight 3566 was travelling to Detroit when the sink in its forward lavatory reportedly sprang a leak. Water began spilling across the floor and flowing down the aisle, soaking the cabin.Concerned that the water could reach the aircraft's electronic systems, the pilots declared an emergency and requested permission to land at Chicago O'Hare International Airport.“Mayday, mayday, mayday,” a pilot told air traffic controllers, according to audio broadcast by LiveATC.net.Explaining the situation, the pilot said: “We’d like to declare an emergency, our forward lav sink has sprung a leak, and it’s spraying so much water that it’s flooding the entire cabin area in the back, and we are worried about electronics.”The crew then requested a diversion to Chicago O'Hare instead of continuing to Detroit.Footage recorded by a passenger and obtained by ABC7 showed water spreading across the aircraft's aisle, leaving a large section of the cabin floor soaked.Images shared by Keegan Morris on Facebook also showed water leaking from the bathroom area and pooling on the floor.The visuals captured the extent of the flooding inside the aircraft, which prompted the pilots to seek an emergency landing over concerns about water reaching the plane's electronics.
Article Summary: Frontier Airlines Flight 3566 was travelling from Denver to Detroit. The sink in its forward lavatory reportedly sprang a leak. Water began spilling across the floor and flowing down the aisle. The pilots requested a diversion to Chicago O'Hare International Airport.

Article Title: Woman killed in New Jersey after driver mistakes her for a garbage bag
Article Text:
The woman reportedly did not stop to check what was on the road (AI image used for representation)

A woman was killed in Newark, New Jersey, after a driver ran her over but allegedly mistook her for a black garbage bag lying on the road. The driver continued to a nearby supermarket and went inside to shop, unaware that the woman was trapped beneath her vehicle.According to a report by NBC Los Angeles, the driver told investigators that she was travelling south on Sherman Avenue when she felt her car hit something. She believed she had struck a black garbage bag and did not stop to check what was on the road.She drove to the a supermarket on Lyons Avenue, parked her vehicle and went inside. When she returned and tried to reverse, the car would not move. She got out to check and discovered the woman lying underneath the vehicle.The driver then alerted a security guard, who contacted emergency services. Police were called to the supermarket parking lot shortly before 7pm (local time) on Friday following the reports of woman trapped under a car.The victim, whose identity has not been made public, was pronounced dead at the scene. Authorities have not disclosed whether the driver will face any charges. The incident remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Woman was killed in Newark, New Jersey, after a driver ran her over. She allegedly mistook her for a black garbage bag lying on the road. The driver continued to a nearby supermarket and went inside to shop. When she returned and tried to reverse, the car would not move. She got out to check and discovered the woman lying underneath the vehicle.

Article Title: Roberto Clemente's three sons sought $45 million after Puerto Rico put the baseball legend's image on commemorative plates; the US Supreme Court refused their appeal on November 9, leaving other claim
Article Text:
Puerto Rican legend Roberto Clemente spent 18 seasons with Pittsburgh, becoming one of baseball's greatest icons.

Supreme Court declines to intervene

How the commemorative plates sparked a dispute

Trademark rights at the centre of the legal battle

Remembering a baseball icon

A sporting legend's legacy can live far beyond the stadium, but deciding who controls that legacy can become a complicated legal battle. More than half a century after Roberto Clemente's death, his name and image have become the subject of a dispute between his family and his native Puerto Rico. In 2022, the US territory issued souvenir license plates featuring the baseball star without his sons' consent, causing a dispute. Now, the US Supreme Court 's refusal to hear their appeal has left the family's fight over trademark rights and compensation unresolved.According to Reuters and ESPN, the Supreme Court declined on November 9 to consider an appeal filed by Clemente's three sons against Puerto Rico's use of their father's likeness on commemorative licence plates and vehicle registration tags.Roberto Clemente Jr, Luis Roberto Clemente and Roberto Enrique Clemente had challenged the programme, arguing that the government had appropriated trademark rights belonging to the family. Their lawsuit, filed alongside two companies they own that work to protect Clemente's brand and philanthropic legacy, sought to prevent future use of his image on vehicle plates.The family also sought $45 million in damages and an additional $3.15 million in compensation for trademark infringement.The sons maintained that the programme generated approximately $15 million for Puerto Rico through the sale of the commemorative registrations.The Supreme Court rejected the appeal without providing an explanation. However, the decision does not resolve every aspect of the wider dispute. According to Reuters, the family's legal representatives intend to continue pursuing the claims that remain before the lower courts.Puerto Rico introduced the special plates and registration tags in 2022 to mark the 50th anniversary of Clemente's death. The designs featured his portrait, his iconic Pittsburgh Pirates jersey number 21 and recognition of his remarkable achievement of recording 3,000 career hits.According to USA Today, the registration programme involved fees of $21 and $5, which collectively generated around $15 million for the territory. The initiative was introduced during a difficult economic period, as Puerto Rico continued recovering from bankruptcy.Clemente's children objected to the arrangement because the revenue went to the government rather than businesses associated with preserving and promoting their father's legacy. The programme was discontinued at the end of 2022.The family subsequently filed a lawsuit, arguing that the unauthorised commercial use of Clemente's identity amounted to a government taking of private property under the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution.The central question concerned whether constitutional protections against government seizure of private property extend automatically to intangible assets such as trademarks.A federal district court in San Juan, presided over by Judge Gina Méndez-Miró, dismissed the family's case. The Boston-based 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals subsequently upheld parts of that decision, rejecting the argument that Puerto Rico's use of the trademarks constituted an unconstitutional taking.According to Reuters and ESPN, the family's lawyers argued before the Supreme Court that the lower courts had weakened constitutional safeguards by treating trademark rights differently from physical property.Puerto Rico claimed the appeals court can protect intangible property under the Constitution. Its legal representatives argued that the decision simply applied existing Supreme Court precedents to the circumstances of the case.The dispute concerns the legacy of one of baseball's most celebrated players. Born in Carolina, Puerto Rico, Clemente spent 18 seasons with the Pittsburgh Pirates between 1955 and 1972.He earned 15 All-Star selections, won two World Series championships and finished his career with exactly 3,000 hits, alongside a .317 batting average, according to USA Today. He was inducted posthumously into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1973.Clemente died on December 31, 1972, aged 38, when the aircraft carrying him humanitarian supplies to earthquake victims in Nicaragua crashed.His sporting achievements and humanitarian contributions have made his identity an enduring part of baseball history. His sons' remaining legal claims mean the dispute over who controls and profits from Clemente's image may continue after the Supreme Court's Nov. 9 decision.Images Courtesy: istock and Roberto Clemente website

Article Title: After moving his hedge fund from Chicago to Miami in 2022, billionaire Ken Griffin bought every one of 138 apartments in a downtown condominium; now he is reshaping the city through massive investment
Article Text: When billionaire hedge fund manager Ken Griffin decided to move his financial empire from Chicago to Miami in 2022, it was seen as another high-profile endorsement of Florida's growing appeal to wealthy investors and businesses. Four years later, his presence in the city has become considerably more significant than anticipated. Griffin has bought all 138 residential apartments in a downtown condominium tower, is backing a multibillion-dollar corporate headquarters and has committed billions to education, healthcare and other causes.According to a Financial Times report, Griffin has spent more than $5.3 billion on property, business infrastructure, philanthropy and political contributions since relocating to South Florida. The Citadel founder's investments have made him one of the most influential private figures in the region, with supporters pointing to the jobs, institutions and development his money could bring.From Chicago to Miami: A financial empire changes baseGriffin announced in June 2022 that Citadel, his hedge fund, and Citadel Securities, its electronic trading business, would move their headquarters from Chicago to Miami.The decision followed years of frustration with conditions in Illinois, including concerns about crime and the state's political leadership. The relocation was expected to take place over several years, with the companies planning to establish a major office presence in Miami's Brickell financial district.The move was not Griffin's first investment in South Florida. He had already shifted some employees to the region during the Covid-19 pandemic and purchased a waterfront property on Star Island. But the headquarters announcement marked a more permanent commitment, bringing the prospect of jobs, business activity and other wealthy financial professionals to the city.His real estate ambitions have since expanded beyond a private residence and office space. In July 2026, Bloomberg reported that Griffin had acquired all 138 residential units at Solaris, a 22-storey condominium tower in Brickell. The purchases were made through a network of limited liability companies, with offers arriving individually and residents initially uncertain about who was behind them.Some owners accepted the offers, while others held out for better prices. The acquisition was part of Griffin's broader effort to assemble property around the site of his planned headquarters. The building's location makes it significant to his wider development plans.A $2.5 billion headquarters and a bigger visionOne of Griffin's largest projects is a new Citadel headquarters in Brickell, estimated to cost about $2.5 billion. The proposed 54-storey development at 1201 Brickell Bay Drive is expected to become a major addition to Miami's skyline. The project is being developed with Related Companies, while Citadel and Citadel Securities plan to occupy a substantial portion of the office space.The headquarters is part of a wider effort to establish Miami as a major centre for financial services. Griffin's relocation has helped attract attention from businesses and wealthy professionals considering South Florida, although the city's growth cannot be attributed to one individual alone.Billions for education, healthcare and researchGriffin's influence extends beyond commercial property. Through his philanthropic initiative, Griffin Catalyst, he has directed substantial sums towards education, medical research and community projects.In September 2026, he announced a gift of more than $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, one of the largest individual donations in the history of higher education. The contribution will help establish a new campus in Miami, while also supporting the university's existing operations in Pittsburgh. The Miami campus is expected to focus on fields including healthcare and biological discovery, national security, energy and climate resilience, and advanced manufacturing.His earlier donations in South Florida include $50 million to the University of Miami's Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center for cancer research and another $50 million to Baptist Health South Florida to support neurological care and research into conditions such as Alzheimer's disease. He also gave $25 million to Nicklaus Children's Hospital for a new surgical tower and supported Miami-Dade public schools, scholarships and community projects.A billionaire's rising influenceBut Griffin's growing role in Miami has also brought scrutiny. The Financial Times report highlighted concerns about political influence, development decisions and the accountability that comes with private wealth shaping public life. His political contributions, which the report puts at more than $60 million, have added to questions about the relationship between wealthy donors and local decision-making.The debate is unfolding as Miami and the wider South Florida region grapple with housing affordability and inequality. The arrival of wealthy residents and businesses has helped fuel investment, but rising housing and living costs have also made it harder for some existing residents to remain in the area.
Article Summary: Hedge fund manager Ken Griffin announced in June 2022 that Citadel, his hedge fund, and Citadel Securities, its electronic trading business, would move their headquarters from Chicago to Miami. Four years later, his presence in the city has become considerably more significant than anticipated. Griffin has spent more than $5.3 billion on property, business infrastructure, philanthropy and political contributions since relocating to South Florida.

Article Title: From fastest passenger ship to world's largest artificial reef: Historic US ocean liner sinks off Florida
Article Text:
The SS United States, a historic ocean liner that carried presidents, celebrities and thousands of passengers, is set for a new life as the world's largest artificial reef.

How was the ship sunk?

Why was the SS United States famous?

A historic US ocean liner, once the fastest passenger ship in the world, was deliberately sunk in the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday to create what is expected to become the world's largest artificial reef.The 990-foot SS United States, which is 108 feet longer than the Titanic, was taken underwater in a controlled operation off the coast of Florida. The $13.5 million project is aimed at turning the former luxury liner into a major destination for divers and fishing enthusiasts, while creating a marine habitat for species such as tuna, marlin and swordfish.The sinking took longer than expected, with much of the ship still visible above the water hours after the operation began. The vessel finally leaned to one side and submerged at around 9 pm local time.“She is an amazing lady who will not lay down without a fight,” Coleen O’Malley, president of Coleen Marine, the company overseeing the sinking, said before the ship disappeared beneath the surface, as quoted by Associated Press. “Much like the amazing nation she was named after.”Officials said the process took longer partly because crews had to fill 128 fuel and lubricant tanks with water to ensure the ship would settle evenly on the ocean floor.“She’s a big ship,” said Nick Tomecek, a spokesperson for Okaloosa County, which helped organise the project.The sinking was carried out without explosives, which officials said could not be used because of federal environmental and explosives regulations. Instead, crews opened the ship's seawater intake system to allow water to flood its hull.Workers had also cut 10-foot-by-10-foot openings in the decks and removed more than 400 portholes in preparation for the operation. The ship is expected to rest in around 180 feet of water, with its top deck approximately 60 feet below the surface, making it accessible to divers.The site is around 25 miles southwest of Destin, Florida, in an area that already has more than 500 artificial reefs.The previous largest artificial reef in the region was the USS Oriskany, a 911-foot aircraft carrier deliberately sunk off Pensacola in 2006. Officials said experienced divers could potentially visit both wrecks in a single day.“We're trying to be the best diving destination in the world,” Tomecek said.The ship was a technological marvel when it made its maiden voyage in 1952. Built by more than 3,000 workers in Virginia, it carried around 1,700 passengers on its first Atlantic crossing, including Margaret Truman, daughter of then US President Harry Truman.During that voyage, it averaged nearly 41 mph (66 kph), breaking the speed record held by Britain's RMS Queen Mary since 1938. The record was set despite the ship encountering a gale with winds reaching 69 mph.At 990 feet, the liner was longer than the Titanic, which sank after hitting an iceberg during its maiden voyage in 1912. Over its career, the SS United States crossed the Atlantic more than 800 times and carried prominent passengers, including Hollywood stars Grace Kelly and Elizabeth Taylor, and presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John F. Kennedy. A young Bill Clinton also travelled aboard the ship in 1968 on his way to Oxford University.Passengers were once served elaborate meals, including caviar, roast duckling and smoked ox tongue.“She really embodies and expresses this country’s best,” said Susan Gibbs, the granddaughter of the ship's designer. “She represents pride and resilience and strength and beauty.”The SS United States was decommissioned in 1969. Later efforts to convert it into a hotel or put it to other commercial uses failed, and it remained docked in Philadelphia from 1996 until recently.The reef project was intended to preserve the vessel rather than see it dismantled for scrap. As part of the preparations, its two 65-foot smokestacks were removed and are expected to become the centrepiece of a museum dedicated to the ship.
Article Summary: The 990-foot SS United States, which is 108 feet longer than the Titanic, was taken underwater in a controlled operation off the coast of Florida. The $13.5 million project is aimed at turning the former luxury liner into a major destination for divers and fishing enthusiasts.

Article Title: Vance considers direct talks with top Iranian security official, as Washington weighs ‘unrealistic’ peace demands
Article Text:
Vice President JD Vance (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

US vice-president JD Vance is reportedly considering face-to-face talks with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei as he takes a leading role in efforts to negotiate an end to the war.According to The Wall Street Journal, which cited US and Middle Eastern officials and people familiar with the discussions, Vance wrote to Rezaei in October requesting a meeting. However, no date has been fixed, and the two sides continue to communicate through mediators and regional allies.President Donald Trump has told senior aides and counterparts in recent days that he is open to Vance resuming negotiations with Iran, and has authorised him to pursue talks, officials told the newspaper. However, discussions about a possible meeting between Vance and Iranian officials are still at a preliminary stage.US officials said the vice-president has lately been more active in Iran diplomacy than special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who are also involved in negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine war.The WSJ reported that Qatar has emerged as a possible venue for the next round of talks. Vance met the Qatari prime minister on Monday, after which the two held discussions with Trump and other White House officials.Efforts to restart negotiations, however, face considerable obstacles. People familiar with Tehran’s position said Iranian officials want Washington to lift its naval blockade, release frozen assets and ease oil sanctions before talks resume. US secretary of state Marco Rubio dismissed these demands as unrealistic, but said Washington would be ready for diplomacy if Iran altered its stance.Mediators have proposed confidence-building measures, including the US moving its aircraft carriers farther away and easing restrictions on Iranian ports. In return, Iran would allow 25 oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, Middle Eastern officials told the newspaper.Doubts persist over whether a deal can be struck. Iranian diplomats fear Trump could still order strikes, while some regional mediators believe Ahmed Vahidi, the hard-line commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, could undermine the negotiations.Rezaei has also hardened his public stance, dismissing reports of possible negotiations as imaginary and saying Iran would not remove any enriched nuclear material from the country.The diplomatic push comes as the Trump administration weighs whether to resume peace talks or maintain its naval blockade and sanctions. On Tuesday, Rubio said the economic pressure campaign was working and that Trump had no immediate need to launch major combat operations, adding that the US military remained prepared to act if Iran crossed any red lines.The WSJ reported that Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller favour maintaining pressure on Tehran rather than rushing into another round of negotiations.
Article Summary: JD Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei in October requesting a meeting. No date has been fixed, and the two sides continue to communicate through mediators and regional allies. Qatar has emerged as a possible venue for the next round of talks.

Article Title: This American town has a single resident and she is the Mayor, bartender and an entire government
Article Text:
Monowi, Nebraska. Image Courtesy: WikiMedia Commons

Elsie Eiler. Image Courtesy: Nebraska Public Media

Who do you think keeps the lights on around here?Being a mayor in Monowi, Nebraska, is a tough job. You have to run the administration, manage the finances, keep the library open and, perhaps most importantly, make sure nobody's glass stays empty for too long. But what happens when you are the only person living in the town you govern?Elsie Eiler is the sole resident of Monowi and the woman keeping the entire town alive. Recognised by Guinness World Records as the incorporated town with the world's lowest population, Monowi is quite literally a one-woman show. And while the title might sound like the beginning of a lonely story, Elsie's life is anything but a tale of someone waiting to be rescued.Monowi was not always this quiet. Like many small American towns, it began as a railway settlement in the early 1900s. The railway brought people, businesses and opportunities, and the village eventually grew into a thriving little community. At its peak in 1930, it had 123 residents. There were shops, restaurants, a school, a post office and even a church. But as the years passed, younger generations moved away in search of jobs and better opportunities elsewhere. Businesses shut down, the railway disappeared and the population steadily declined.By 1980, only 18 people remained.By 2000, the town had just two residents, Elsie and her husband, Rudy Eiler. A world where it seems its just me and my partner sounds like a dream come true, right? The two had known each other since childhood, having met at the local one-room schoolhouse. They eventually married and settled in Monowi, where they built their lives together. They also purchased the local tavern in 1971, turning it into a familiar meeting place for people in the surrounding area.Unfortunately, when Rudy passed away in 2004, Elsie was left as the town's only inhabitant. While many might have considered moving somewhere with more people around, she decided to stay. This was her home, after all.And she wasn't about to let her husband's memory disappear either. Rudy was an avid reader who had accumulated around 5,000 books over the years. In 2005, Elsie established Rudy's Library in his memory, using his personal collection to create a little public library in the village. Today, it remains one of the three active buildings in Monowi, alongside her home and the tavern. The library operates on an honour system, allowing visitors to browse and borrow books without the usual fuss of library cards and administrative formalities.Running a town of one also comes with its fair share of paperwork. As mayor, Elsie handles the municipal administration, prepares the town's road plans, manages its finances and applies for the funding needed to maintain basic services. She also serves as the town clerk, secretary and treasurer. And then there is her other rather interesting responsibility: issuing herself the annual liquor licence for the tavern she owns and operates. The application goes through the village secretary, who happens to be Elsie. She signs it as the clerk and receives it as the business owner. Getting things done without having to chase anyone for an approval is a dream job; she truly is her own boss!But her administrative duties are only part of her day. At 93, Elsie continues to work at the Monowi Tavern for around 12 hours a day, six days a week. She serves coffee, cooks burgers, pours drinks and welcomes anyone who happens to walk through the door. Her customers include local farmers, regulars from neighbouring towns and curious travellers who have made the journey just to meet the woman behind the town's unusual record.In fact, visitors have arrived from all 50 US states and more than 60 countries. The tavern has become something of a tourist attraction, with people eager to see the famous village sign announcing its population of one. Yet Elsie doesn't seem particularly impressed by her international popularity. She has always been more interested in the people who actually come through the door than the headlines written about her.In Monowi, a neighbour isn't 4 feet apart, but 40 miles away, as she once explained to Country Living. You know how they say, good fences make good neighbours. But, that doesn’t mean the relationship is distant. Instead it is more cordial than ever. Everyone looks out for one another. When it snows, a local farmer might turn up to clear her parking lot and the main street. When the tavern gets busy, friends and acquaintances are happy to lend a hand.During winter, regulars gather at the tavern on Sunday evenings to play euchre, a card game, and spend time catching up. Some customers have known Elsie for decades. Others are younger generations of families who have been visiting the establishment for years. It is a place where people share meals, stories and a little company after a long day. As Matthew 22:39 says, you shall love your neighbor as yourself.This is not a rescue call, not a 'One Less Lonely Girl' storyline waiting to happen. Elsie doesn't need rescuing, and being the only person living in a town doesn't necessarily mean being alone in the world. She has family, friends, familiar faces and a community that continues to show up for her. Her daughter, Rene Lassise, has pointed out that outsiders often miss the camaraderie and genuine connections that keep her mother attached to the place. The town might have only one official resident, but it certainly has more than one person who considers it home.Of course, even Elsie knows that Monowi's future is uncertain. With nobody else living there to take over the administrative responsibilities or keep its businesses running, the town's existence is closely tied to her own. She has admitted that thinking about a time when she might no longer be able to stay makes her sad. She would like to see Monowi continue to exist rather than become another collection of abandoned buildings along a roadside.It is a rather unusual situation. Most people spend their lives looking for somewhere to belong, while Elsie has spent hers holding on to a place that the rest of the world slowly moved away from. Perhaps a town isn't always defined by how many people live in it, how many shops line its streets or how busy its roads are. Sometimes, it is defined by the people who keep showing up, the stories they share and the connections they refuse to let go of.So, who keeps the lights on around here? Well, the mayor does. And she might just be serving you a burger while she is at it. And maybe, this town ain't big enough for two.
Article Summary: Elsie Eiler is the sole resident of Monowi, Nebraska. Recognised by Guinness World Records as the incorporated town with the world's lowest population. As mayor, Elsie handles the municipal administration, prepares the town's road plans, manages its finances and applies for the funding.
