Noise complaints and more

The Oklahoma Supreme Court has upheld a lower court ruling against an Edmond homeowner who used his property for short-term rentals, finding that the practice violated the Silverhawk community’s restrictive covenants. The decision closes a dispute that began in 2019, when the man started renting out his home to guests, contrary to the homeowners’ association (HOA) rules. In a decision on 11 November, the court upheld the injunction barring short-term rentals and the $8,528 in fines imposed by the association.The man bought the house in the Silverhawk neighbourhood of Edmond, Oklahoma, in 2015. A few years later, he began renting it to short-term guests through platforms such as Airbnb. The man claims he consulted the board before renting out the property. In October 2019, he contacted the neighbourhood association about renting out the house. ‘I don't see anything that stops you from doing that,’ one board member reportedly told him. That, however, was not an approval. The man argues that he did not interpret the response as a refusal. ‘But I didn't feel her response was explicit enough to tell me that, so that's why I took my next step.’He emailed the group's secretary, who replied that the association did not restrict rentals. The man therefore took that as the answer he needed.The HOA's rules were clear in some respects. They stated that the lots ‘shall be used for private residence purposes only’. They also specified that ‘no store or business’ could be built or maintained on any lot. However, nothing in the wording specifically mentioned renting to visitors for a few nights. The association argued that renting a property for money to a rotating group of guests constituted a business. The man argued that the term was too vague to be enforced against him.When the dispute went to trial, a neighbour who lives directly behind the house described weekend groups using the backyard grill, some as large as fourteen people. She said the noise could reach her bedrooms as late as two or three in the morning. Another neighbour described large parties and more cars than a typical family would own. The man questioned both witnesses and pointed out that neither had complained to him directly or contacted the police. The trial court weighed their testimony, and the Supreme Court later said it would not second-guess that judgement.The Oklahoma County District Court heard the case in a five-day bench trial. The judge ruled that the rentals breached the covenant. The court issued an injunction against the business, awarded the association fines and assessments, and rejected the man's claim that the association had breached its contract with him. He represented himself.Unhappy with the decision, the man appealed. The Court of Civil Appeals, in a divided ruling, reversed much of that decision. The HOA took the matter to the Oklahoma Supreme Court. Five justices joined the majority opinion by Justice Edmondson, which vacated the appeals court's decision and affirmed the trial court's judgement. The majority said the covenant's language was clear and that the ordinary meaning of ‘business’ applied to property rules just as it did to contracts and tax law.Four justices dissented. They argued that the word ‘business’ describes what a building is used for, not how people occupy it. The dissent said guests who sleep, cook and grill at a house are living there as a home, even for a short time, and that the court should not add a rule that the covenant never states.The court also declined to review the attorney's fee award because the man had not raised the issue in the proper manner. This means the trial court's decision on fees remains in place.However, the homeowner's frustration has not faded following the ruling. ‘Over five exhausting years, the very institutions meant to protect homeowners betrayed me,’ he told NonDoc, a local news outlet that covered the case. He said he had to file for bankruptcy to protect his home.
Article Summary: The man bought the house in the Silverhawk neighbourhood of Edmond, Oklahoma, in 2015. A few years later, he began renting it to short-term guests through platforms such as Airbnb. In October 2019, he contacted the neighbourhood association about renting out the house. The association argued that renting a property for money to a rotating group of guests constituted a business. The man argued that the term was too vague to be enforced against him.

Article Title: Between 1942 and 1977, Shenandoah National Park ranger Roy Sullivan was struck by lightning seven times and survived each one, a feat that earned him a Guinness World Record for most lightning strikes
Article Text:
A series of increasingly bizarre encounters

The seventh strike and a world record

A shocking tale

A lightning strike is usually a terrifying, potentially fatal encounter. For Roy Sullivan, it became an extraordinary recurring experience. The Virginia park ranger was struck by lightning seven times between 1942 and 1977, surviving every incident and earning a place in Guinness World Records as the person who survived the most lightning strikes. His encounters left him with burns, singed hair and injuries, and eventually earned him the nickname “Spark Ranger”, according to Guinness World Records.Sullivan’s first brush with lightning came in April 1942, when he was working at Shenandoah National Park in Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains. He was at a fire lookout tower when a storm set the structure ablaze. As he attempted to escape, lightning struck him in the right leg. The bolt left a scorch mark, tore through his boot and damaged the nail on his big toe.It was an experience that might have made most people wary of storms for the rest of their lives. Sullivan, though, would encounter lightning six more times over the next 35 years.For 27 years after the first incident, Sullivan reportedly went without another strike. That changed in July 1969, when he was driving his truck along a mountain road during a storm. Lightning struck trees nearby before travelling through the vehicle’s open windows. Sullivan was knocked unconscious, his eyebrows were burned and his wristwatch was damaged.The following year, in July 1970, lightning struck him while he was tending to his garden. The bolt reportedly burned his left shoulder and threw him off his feet. In April 1972, another strike hit while he was working inside a park guardhouse. His hair caught fire, forcing him to put it out with water.By then, Sullivan had begun taking precautions. According to a 2013 Washington Post profile, he carried water with him after the incident in which his hair caught fire. But avoiding storms and taking shelter did not appear to end his extraordinary run of misfortune.On August 7, 1973, lightning struck him again while he was driving. Sullivan later said he had stopped after trying to get away from a storm, only to see a bolt coming towards him. The strike set his hair alight, burned his legs and reportedly knocked him out of his vehicle.The sixth incident occurred on June 5, 1976, while Sullivan was walking along a trail. He suffered an ankle injury and his hair was burned once more. Five months later, he retired from the National Park Service. He and his wife moved to a property near Waynesboro, Virginia, where he installed copper lightning rods around his home, including on the trailer, television antenna and nearby trees. Still, the precautions did not bring his encounters to an end.On June 25, 1977, Sullivan was fishing when lightning struck him for the seventh time. He reportedly smelled sulphur and felt the hair on his arms stand up moments before the bolt hit. The strike burned his chest and stomach, singed his hair and damaged his hearing in one ear. He managed to reach his car and return home, after which he was taken to hospital.Guinness World Records lists this as his final lightning strike. Its record entry documents seven incidents, beginning in 1942 and ending on June 25, 1977. Sullivan was subsequently recognised as the person who had survived the most lightning strikes.His story attracted attention well beyond the national park. He appeared on television programmes and became a familiar name in accounts of unusual survival stories. The nickname “Spark Ranger” followed him, while his lightning-damaged hat and wristwatch became part of the lore surrounding his experiences.Sullivan’s record is recognised by Guinness World Records, but the details of his encounters have also attracted questions. A 2013 investigation by The Washington Post noted that none of the seven strikes was directly witnessed by another person. His wife and fellow rangers were not present for the incidents, and there was no medical record independently confirming every strike.The report found that newspaper accounts and statements from people who knew Sullivan offered some support for his injuries. His family doctor and a former park superintendent were said to have verified injuries, though not necessarily the lightning strikes themselves. A retired National Park Service historian interviewed for the report expressed confidence in the Guinness record, while others who knew Sullivan were more cautious.Sullivan died in September 1983, aged 71. His story remains an unusual chapter in the history of Shenandoah National Park and a reminder of the unpredictable power of thunderstorms.
Article Summary: Roy Sullivan was struck by lightning seven times between 1942 and 1977. His encounters left him with burns, singed hair and injuries. He earned a place in Guinness World Records as the person who survived the most lightning strikes. His story attracted attention well beyond the national park.

Article Title: A Colorado delivery driver who cares for her 82-year-old mother apologised at a door for a mixed-up pizza order, the family came out and prayed with her, and strangers have since donated over $76,000
Article Text:
The family chose not to focus on the delivery mix-up (Screengrab)

Family starts fundraiser with Metcalf's permission

Pastor speaks about the response to the video

More than $76,000 has been raised for a Colorado woman who works as a pizza delivery driver while looking after her 82-year-old mother. The fundraising campaign began after a family she delivered an order to learnt about her responsibilities and decided to help her.Suzanna Metcalf's situation came to public attention after a brief interaction at the home of Pastor Neal Seiwert in Castle Rock, Colorado, Good News Network reported. She had arrived with an incorrect pizza order and apologised to the family. She told them she would have to return with the correct order and blamed the mistake on getting old.The family chose not to focus on the delivery mix-up. Seiwert, his wife Hailee and their three young daughters stepped outside to pray with Metcalf. They placed their hands on her shoulders during the prayer. The interaction was recorded by a doorbell camera.The video was later shared online by Seiwert and reached millions of viewers. Its popularity brought attention to Metcalf's circumstances, particularly the responsibilities she manages outside her delivery job.She works delivery shifts while serving as the full-time caregiver for her 82-year-old mother.Her responsibilities include managing her mother's daily care and medical needs, as well as household expenses. The Seiwert family decided to extend their support beyond the prayer after learning more about her situation.After the video attracted widespread attention, the Seiwerts managed to locate Metcalf. They then approached her about starting a fundraising campaign and received her permission to do so.The GoFundMe page described Metcalf as a woman who had spent years putting others first. The family set an initial target of $10,000, hoping to provide some financial assistance as she continued looking after her mother.However, contributions continued to arrive well beyond that target. More than 2,600 donors have contributed to the campaign over the past year. The total has now crossed $76,000.The money is intended to give Metcalf some financial breathing room while she manages her caregiving duties and delivery work. The campaign's response followed the widespread circulation of the doorbell camera footage.Seiwert later discussed the incident with the New York Post. He said his family wanted Metcalf to know that they were there to support her and that other people valued her efforts too.He also spoke about the emotional response from people who watched the recording. “So many people are commenting on how it brought them to tears. There are many people who simply just need love,” he said.
Article Summary: Suzanna Metcalf works as a pizza delivery driver while looking after her 82-year-old mother. Her situation came to public attention after a brief interaction at the home of Pastor Neal Seiwert in Castle Rock, Colorado. She had arrived with an incorrect pizza order and apologised to the family. The video was later shared online and reached millions of viewers.

Article Title: India-born Praneet Menon wins Vermont state House seat in US election
Article Text:
Praneeth Menon was elected to the Vermont House of Representatives from the Orleans-Lamoille district. (Pic Credit: Agency)

Indian-origin candidate Praneeth Menon has been elected to the Vermont house of representatives from the Orleans-Lamoille district in the United States, contesting as a joint nominee backed by both the Republican and Democratic parties.The district elects two representatives, with the top two candidates securing seats. In the recent election, incumbent Mark Higley emerged as the leading candidate with 2,815 votes, while Menon finished second with 1,992 votes. Both were consequently elected to the state legislature.Menon initially entered the electoral race as a republican candidate before securing the endorsement of both major political parties.His campaign focused on issues affecting local communities, particularly the rising cost of living for rural families, shortages of resources in schools, housing affordability, healthcare access, job creation and labour shortages.He also advocated greater scrutiny of property taxes and utility bills, alongside measures to support small businesses, strengthen vocational education and improve broadband connectivity.His campaign was built around the slogan, “Responsible leadership, practical action”.Born and raised in India, Menon moved to the United States at the age of 16 to pursue higher education. He studied aeronautical and mechanical engineering at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute before completing a master's degree at the University of Vermont.Menon has professional experience in the aviation and defence sectors, having worked on projects for the US air force and Army. His career has also included roles as a flight instructor and software entrepreneur.In addition to his professional experience, he has been involved in local governance, serving on the town's planning commission and finance committee.
Article Summary: Praneeth Menon was elected to the Vermont House of Representatives from the Orleans-Lamoille district. He was backed by both the Republican and Democratic parties. His campaign was built around the slogan, ‘Responsible leadership, practical action’

Article Title: In 1984, Paul Newman gave his Rolex to his daughter’s boyfriend, saying it “tells pretty good time”; 33 years later, it sold for $17.75 million
Article Text:
A Rolex Cosmograph Daytona. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Joanne Woodward gave the

Daytona

to Newman in 1968

Cox met Nell Newman in the fall of 1983 at College of the Atlantic

Portrait of Paul Newman. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The watch seemed to vanish after 1984

The Daytona sold for $17,752,500 on October 26, 2017

A portion of the proceeds went to Nell Newman’s foundation and Newman’s Own Foundation

A casual question about the time on a Connecticut riverbank led to one of the best-known watch sales in history. In the summer of 1984, Paul Newman asked his daughter Nell’s boyfriend, James Cox, what time it was. Cox said he did not own a watch, so Newman handed him the Rolex on his own wrist. Cox kept the watch for roughly 33 years. In October 2017, he and Nell Newman consigned it to Phillips in New York, where it set a world record for a wristwatch at auction. Newman had died in 2008 and never saw the resale.The watch was a gift from his wife. UPI reported that Joanne Woodward gave him the Cosmosgraph Daytona in 1968. The case back was engraved “Drive Carefully, Me”, a nod to Newman’s racing. Newman put it to work. He timed races with it and bet friends that it ran more accurately than theirs, a habit Phillips has described in its sale notes. He would call the speaking clock, a phone line that gave the exact time, to get his money. Phillips also indicated that he wore this watch daily from 1969 to 1984.The two started dating while they were both still fellow students.She went by the name Nell Potts in school, but hid her association with her family. According to Phillips, the girl only came clean about her surname after listening to a particular story. In the summer of 1984, the two were staying at their family estate in Westport, Connecticut. In her letter to Cox that accompanied the watch, Nell stated that her father went to the riverbank to see how James was doing. One day he asked Cox what the time was and Cox told him he did not know and had no watch. Newman gifted him the Rolex and explained that all he needed to do was to wind it daily and then “it tells pretty good time”.In some versions of the story, the quote has changed to “keeps good time”, which is the version published in City AM. UPI also mentioned that Cox had responded to the question “a hair past a freckle,” his way of saying he had no watch.Collectors were completely oblivious about the whereabouts of the watch. According to Autoblog, it appears to have been lost in 1984 when Newman got a new Daytona watch from his wife. NBC Los Angeles also says that the watch went off the radar and was assumed missing, following the death of Paul Newman in 2008. All along, Cox owned it. It is said by Phillips to be one of the greatest mysteries in horology that was only solved when Cox came forward.The watch was auctioned by Phillips in New York on October 26, 2017. According to Phillips, the 1968 Cosmograph Daytona Reference 6239 reached a hammer price of $15.5 million. Phillips claimed that their final price was $17,752,500, including the buyer’s premium and thus they achieved a world record for an auctioned wristwatch. As stated by Hodinkee, the former recorded for the most expensive wristwatch, which sold for approximately $11.1 million in 2016, was held by the steel Patek Philippe Reference 1518. That made the Newman Daytona about 60 percent more expensive.The watch was listed for sale by both Cox and Nell together and according to UPI, Cox is the treasurer of the Newman Foundation. According to the report by KOMO News, Cox was going to donate a major part of the money he earns to the Newman Foundation. The Newman Daytona held the record for just over two years, from Phillips’ sale on October 26, 2017 to the Christie’s Geneva auction on November 9, 2019. Christie's reported that on November 9, 2019, the steel Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime Reference 6300A-010 sold for 31 million Swiss francs, about $31.3 million, at the Only Watch charity auction at Christie’s Geneva. The same report also notes that the price topped the Newman Rolex’s $17.8 million. The Newman Daytona still ranks as the most expensive Rolex sold at auction.
Article Summary: The Rolex Cosmograph Daytona sold for $17,752,500 on October 26, 2017 at Phillips in New York. The watch was a gift from Paul Newman's wife, Joanne Woodward, in 1968. In the summer of 1984, Newman asked his daughter Nell’s boyfriend, James Cox, what time it was. Cox said he did not own a watch, so Newman handed him the Rolex on his own wrist. Cox kept the watch for roughly 33 years.

Article Title: Pakistan announces schedule for Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations despite Attari-Wagah closure
Article Text:
Pakistan has maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side (Photo: PTI).

AMRITSAR: Despite the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah international land border following Operation Sindoor, the Pakistan government has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev, expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib.Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side, although pilgrim movement through it continues to be suspended by India.According to Pak media reports, the programme was finalised at a meeting of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC), chaired by its president and Punjab provincial minister for minority affairs and human rights, Ramesh Singh Arora, to review arrangements for the celebrations.As per the schedule, Indian Sikh pilgrims are expected to arrive in Pakistan through the Attari international border on November 22. The main ceremony will be held on November 24 at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev. The pilgrims are scheduled to return on December 1.Reacting to Pakistan’s announcement, Sikh scholar Jagdeep Singh said the proposed pilgrimage programme assumes significance amid strained India-Pakistan ties and the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah border after Operation Sindoor.“Keeping the border open would serve the interests of both countries and, above all, make it easier for devotees to visit their historic religious shrines,” said Jagdeep.Interestingly, while Pakistan maintains that the Kartarpur corridor is operational on its side and has expressed readiness to facilitate Sikh devotees, India has suspended pilgrim movement through it since May 2025.In a statement, Arora said Pakistani diplomatic missions had been instructed to facilitate visa issuance for Sikh pilgrims. He also urged India to allow the Sikh sangat to visit its historic shrines.According to reports, the arrangements reviewed at the meeting include air-conditioned buses, accommodation, langar, medical facilities, mineral water and currency exchange services. A Rescue 1122 ambulance will accompany every convoy of 20 buses to meet medical emergencies.
Article Summary: Pakistan has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev. It is expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib. Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side.

Article Title: 'Two eight-year-olds or four four-year-olds': Pakistani cleric's child bride 'joke' sparks outrage
Article Text:
Mufti Tariq Masood (Source: Wikimedia Commons)

Education and women's autonomy

Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage.In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.One of the remarks highlighted in the report came from a viral video in which Masood joked that if someone could not find a 16-year-old bride, he could provide “two eight-year-olds” or “four four-year-olds”. The comment drew criticism from people who said it trivialised child marriage and normalised the sexualisation of minors.The Daily Mirror said the backlash was dismissed by supporters as a misunderstanding, with the remark defended as a joke taken out of context.The newspaper also pointed to Masood's repeated opposition to statutory minimum marriage-age laws. According to the report, he has argued that Islamic jurisprudence does not prescribe a universal minimum age of 18 and that parents or guardians should retain discretion over when a girl marries.A recurring theme in his sermons, the newspaper said, is the emphasis on physical development and perceived maturity rather than chronological age when determining whether a girl is ready for marriage. The preacher had made remarks discussing the physical suitability of girls aged nine and ten in the context of marital relations. Pakistan as a country has been grappling with child sexual abuse, forced marriages and gender equality and positioning such leaders as popular figures raises extreme concerns.The Daily Mirror also highlighted Masood's remarks on women's education, saying that some of his statements appear to place a husband's authority above a young wife's decision to continue her studies.It further cited comments about women marrying late, including references to them becoming “aunties”, and discussions of the benefits husbands derive from marriage.Masood has also been criticised for presenting early marriage as a way to manage men's sexual desiresMasood's sermons have reportedly become difficult to access after copyright complaints and takedown requests. Critics have alleged that this limits public scrutiny of his statements, while his supporters maintain that some remarks are circulated without their original context.Masood has built a substantial following on YouTube, Facebook and other social media platforms through a preaching style that combines religious instruction with informal language and humour. His reach extends beyond traditional religious institutions, particularly among younger and urban audiences.
Article Summary: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage. In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.

Article Title: Pakistan militant attack kills 10 policemen in KPK's Kohat, gunbattle still under way
Article Text:
No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. (FIle photo)

At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Wednesday, officials told news agency AP.The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire between the attackers and security forces, local police official Faisal Khan said.Khan confirmed that two senior police officers were among those killed. He added that the gunbattle was still underway, but did not share further details.No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. However, suspicion is likely to centre on the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, which has intensified its attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.Pakistan has witnessed a rise in militant violence over the past few years, with much of it attributed to the TTP. The group is separate from the Afghan Taliban but shares close ties with it. The Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.Islamabad has repeatedly accused Afghanistan's Taliban-led government of providing shelter to TTP fighters operating against Pakistan. Kabul has denied the allegations.
Article Summary: At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire. No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far.

Article Title: Pakistan court frames charges against 8, including grandson of deputy PM Ishaq Dar, in gang rape case
Article Text:
Pakistan deput​y PM Ishaq Dar (File photo)​​

A Pakistani court on Wednesday framed charges against eight suspects, including the grandson of deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, in connection with the gang rape of two foreign women , an official said.All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty, the official added.“Lahore court judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty. He directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on December 9 so that the formal trial proceedings could begin,” the official said.Earlier, police in Pakistan's Punjab province had cleared Raza Dar and his four accomplices of charges in the case, instead charging three other employees of Ishaq Dar's grandson of raping the women.The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela. They were allegedly kidnapped and raped by Raza Dar and his four friends after arriving in Lahore on a business trip in June. Medical examinations confirmed that the women had been raped. They returned to their respective countries after recording their statements.According to the police report, the women met Raza Dar in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business.After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested more than $500,000. However, the women allegedly failed to provide further returns or repay the amount.In June, Raza Dar invited the women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They initially stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to the hill station of Murree voluntarily.The women were later taken to a house in Lahore's Defence Housing Authority, where they were allegedly held captive and pressured to repay the money. They were forced to transfer $19,500, as per the police report.Armed men guarded the women and threatened them with a knife, a gun and a broken piece of mirror. They also threatened to kill them and sell their body parts if they failed to meet the demands.The women eventually managed to escape after the vehicle in which their alleged captors were taking them to Lahore airport met with an accident.
Article Summary: Pakistani court frames charges against eight suspects in gang rape of two foreign women. All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty. The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela.

Article Title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan taken to hospital for eye check-up, treatment; shifted back to Adiala Jail
Article Text:
Imran Khan's health sparks concern

Qureshi also hospitalised

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison, news agency Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing officials.Khan, who is lodged in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), where he also received treatment for blood pressure-related issues, one of the officials said."He had some blood pressure issues ... and was given required treatment last night. He has been shifted back to his prison cell," the person said.The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years after losing power in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging that they are politically motivated. The Shehbaz Sharif government has rejected his claims.All but one of Khan's convictions have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending.His lawyers have repeatedly raised concerns over his health in prison, claiming that his condition has deteriorated and that he has lost significant vision in his right eye.Wednesday's hospital visit is the first known instance of Khan being taken for treatment and subsequently returned to jail since August, when an earlier hospital visit was cut short.Meanwhile, a Pakistani court has directed jail authorities to allow Khan's legal team to meet him and his wife, his party said.Khan's hospital visit comes a day after his close aide and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) deputy chairman, Shah Mahmood Qureshi, was taken to a hospital in Lahore after collapsing inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail.According to a prison official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old former foreign minister was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment and remains hospitalised.Khan, who led Pakistan to its maiden ODI World Cup title in 1992, has been behind bars for more than three years. Concerns over his health and prison conditions have repeatedly been raised by his family, party members and supporters, including former international cricket colleagues.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison. The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging they are politically motivated.

Article Text: More debt, less development? Pakistan spends just 10% of annual budget

Article Title: Imran Khan aide, ex-Pakistan foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi collapses in jail; hospitalised
Article Text:
(With PTI inputs)

Pakistan's former foreign minister and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf vice-chairman Shah Mahmood Qureshi was admitted to a hospital after collapsing in his barrack at a jail in Lahore, a prison official said on Tuesday.According to the official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old leader was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment, the official added.Qureshi has been in jail since August 2023 in multiple cases linked to the May 9, 2023, riots, when Tehreek-i-Insaf supporters went on a rampage following the arrest of party chairman and former Prime Minister Imran Khan.Qureshi's counsel, Rana Mudassar Umar, confirmed that the veteran politician was taken to hospital after fainting and suffering a fall.Umar added that the PTI leader would remain under observation for 24 hours, after which doctors would decide whether he should continue treatment at the hospital or be shifted back to jail.Meanwhile, Qureshi's daughter alleged that her father had been jailed on "trumped-up" charges and accused the federal government of keeping him behind bars with "malafide" intent."Three and a half years ago, a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped-up charges. He not only fought the cypher case with resolve and courage but refused to sacrifice his principles at the altar of self-interest," Mehr Bano said."My father has been acquitted multiple times but remains behind bars due to the government's malafide. Over 90 bail hearings have gone by, but the record has yet to be produced. A man whose innocence has been proven again and again is being held... It is high time the judge establishes his authority and grants him bail," she demanded.Bano also highlighted her father's more than four decades of public service in Pakistan."He has served twice as Pakistan's foreign minister, and as parliamentary leader and vice-chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, he has fulfilled important responsibilities and protected Pakistan's interests. He has fought for the supremacy of the Constitution and democracy. He deserves justice and freedom," she stated.
Article Summary: Pakistan's former foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi was admitted to a hospital after collapsing in his barrack at a jail in Lahore. The 70-year-old has been in jail since August 2023 in multiple cases linked to the May 9, 2023, riots. His daughter has accused the federal government of keeping him behind bars with "malafide" intent.

Article Title: Lashkar terrorist Hafiz Saeed's political outfit loses Pakistan's parliamentary bypoll
Article Text:
Terrorist Hafiz Saeed was previously associated with the Milli Muslim League.

A political party linked to Mumbai terror attack mastermind Hafiz Saeed has suffered a defeat in a parliamentary by-election in Pakistan, with the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) retaining the seat.The contest took place on Sunday in the NA-77 constituency of Gujranwala district in Punjab, around 80 km from Lahore. The by-election was necessitated by the death of sitting lawmaker Mehmood Bashir Virk.According to results announced by the Election Commission on Monday, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar secured more than 30,000 votes. However, he was defeated by PML-N's Rashid Bashir Virk, who polled over 43,000 votes.The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, the Pakistan Peoples Party and Jamaat-e-Islami did not contest the by-election.The polling saw a low voter turnout and was accompanied by allegations of electoral malpractice. Voters in one village boycotted the election entirely, while five PML-N women lawmakers were issued notices seeking explanations over alleged violations of the election code of conduct.Rejecting the outcome, the PMML accused the ruling PML-N of widespread rigging and refused to accept the results.The party had also contested Pakistan's 2024 general elections but failed to win a single seat.Hafiz Saeed, who founded the banned terrorist outfits Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jamaat-ud-Dawa, was previously associated with the Milli Muslim League. The PMML later emerged as another political platform linked to him and reportedly enjoys the backing of Pakistan's establishment.
Article Summary: The contest took place on Sunday in the NA-77 constituency of Gujranwala district in Punjab, around 80 km from Lahore. The by-election was necessitated by the death of sitting lawmaker Mehmood Bashir Virk. Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar secured more than 30,000 votes.

Article Title: Pakistani TV anchor Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home; police probe husband's claim of accidental firing
Article Text:
Pakistani TV anchorperson Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home in Rawalpindi

First Lady condemns killing, calls for transparent probe

A Pakistani television anchorperson, Rabia Ahsan, was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday, with police taking her husband into custody and seizing the suspected weapon, Pakistani media outlet Samaa reported.The incident took place in the Gulshanabad area of the city, where Ahsan worked as an anchor and programme host for a local private TV channel.City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera confirmed that Ahsan's husband had been detained and that the suspected weapon had been seized. He said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding her death.According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that Ahsan's husband had claimed the gunshot was fired accidentally.Sukhera visited the crime scene along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations, the SSP investigations and a team of forensic experts. Teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) were collecting evidence from the house.The body was being taken to a hospital for a postmortem examination. Sukhera said a case was being registered and the investigation would be conducted on merit.Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness over Ahsan's killing and strongly condemned the violence.She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable, according to a statement issued by the Presidency.Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concern over what she described as a “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.She recalled the murder of Hina Javed, a 45-year-old digital media executive who was found dead at her Rawalpindi residence in August with signs of torture.The First Lady noted that the outcome of the investigation into Javed's murder was still awaited.
Article Summary: Rabia Ahsan was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday. Police took her husband into custody and seized the suspected weapon. Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari condemned the killing.

Article Title: Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans faceless anti-terror courts: Report
Article Text:
Faceless terror courts, Rs 70bn police boost planned in Pakistan’s KP (Reuters photo)

Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province plans to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts to protect witnesses, prosecutors and judges involved in terrorism cases, according to a report by Dawn on Sunday.The provincial administration also plans to allocate 70 billion Pakistani rupees annually to the police and Counter-Terrorism Department to strengthen their capabilities, the report said.The developments come less than a month after Pakistan's federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, accusing the provincial government led by former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of failing to engage in the fight against terrorism.Under the move, the chief minister and provincial cabinet ceased to hold office, with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi assuming executive authority with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council.Both the national assembly and senate approved the emergency on October 14, while a joint sitting of Parliament endorsed the emergency and governor's rule the following day.At a televised briefing on Sunday, Home Secretary Amjad Ali Khan said an amendment had been sent to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts.He said witnesses were reluctant to testify in terrorism cases because of fears for their safety. The proposed system would also protect prosecutors and judges, *Dawn* quoted him as saying.Khan said the administration planned to allocate 59.8 billion Pakistani rupees to the police and 10.3 billion Pakistani rupees to the Counter-Terrorism Department, with funds earmarked for infrastructure and equipment.The plans also include strengthening police stations and checkpoints, expanding the Safe City project and installing anti-drone systems in Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat and Bannu, the report said.Khan said the province faced a shortage of more than 10,000 police personnel and lacked adequate security infrastructure, particularly in the merged districts. He also flagged weak counter-drone capabilities, noting that militants were increasingly using drone technology.The administration plans to intensify intelligence-based operations, arrest terrorist facilitators, re-verify people placed on Pakistan's Fourth Schedule and mobilise the Rapid Response Force, Khan said.It also plans to deploy artificial intelligence tools to monitor social media and counter terrorist narratives, while satellite communication systems will be installed in areas with inadequate connectivity.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor Kundi, who attended the briefing, said restoring peace and strengthening the police were the administration's priorities. He said development could follow only after security was restored and called for greater political ownership of the fight against terrorism.Kundi said the police would be provided with weapons, ammunition and other resources, while facilities in the merged districts would also be improved. He said groups taking up arms against the state could not be offered dialogue and would be dealt with accordingly, Dawn reported.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province plans to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts to protect witnesses, prosecutors and judges involved in terrorism cases. The provincial administration also plans to allocate 70 billion Pakistani rupees annually to the police and Counter-Terrorism Department.

Article Title: Balochistan Parties call statewide shutdown in mid-November as crisis deepens in troubled province
Article Text:
(Representative image) (Photo: ANI).

Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19, to be followed by demonstrations at district headquarters. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns.The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, according to a report by The Express Tribune cited by ANI. ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai chaired the meeting, which was attended by representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and several other political groups. The participants agreed to bring their joint political and democratic efforts under a coordinated movement to raise public grievances.In a joint declaration, the parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming. They cited persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised the unresolved issue of missing persons, and highlighted the difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways.The parties pointed to rising unemployment and economic decline. They blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for disrupting economic activity across the province. Soaring inflation, prolonged power and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on the supply of essential agricultural inputs, including urea fertiliser, were also cited. According to The Express Tribune, the leaders said these issues had adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment.The participating parties also criticised the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to ensure public safety, maintain law and order, protect natural resources and restore economic stability.Furthermore, the parties announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to decide the next course of action. An all-parties conference will be held in the first week of December to take Balochistan’s concerns to the national leadership.
Article Summary: Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns. The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP)

Article Title: 'If he wishes to come’: Pakistan open to considering visa for Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s Lahore visit
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27, following an invitation to the event.Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing while responding to a question about Mann's possible visit, PTI reported."The government would consider issuing Mann a visa if he wishes to visit Pakistan. However, whether the Indian government permits him to travel is an entirely separate matter," he told reporters in Islamabad.On October 23, Mann had said that he had received an invitation to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore.However, the Punjab chief minister also raised doubts over whether he would be permitted to travel to Pakistan.“Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he remarked.Mann had also voiced his wish for all members of the Punjab legislative assembly to visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if it reopened.The corridor, which links Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims visiting the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.It enables Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without a Pakistani visa, subject to applicable arrangements.The corridor has remained closed to pilgrims travelling from the India since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.Last month, the Centre denied political clearance to Mann for his visit to Paris, prompting the Punjab government to challenge the decision before the Punjab and Haryana high court.The high court subsequently cleared his visit, observing that the Centre had “not explained” the political considerations it cited while refusing permission for his trip to the French capital.
Article Summary: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27. Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing.

Article Title: Pakistan’s forex rises by record $ 110 million in just a week despite West Asia crisis
Article Text:
Pakistan’s central bank reported a $110 million weekly rise in foreign exchange reserves, taking total holdings to a record $26.864 billion

Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $110 million in a week to a record $26.864 billion, according to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), even as the West Asia conflict continues to disrupt global energy markets and push up oil prices.In a statement on Thursday, the central bank said the country's total reserves had increased from $26.754 billion in the previous week.The rise included a $39 million increase in SBP-held reserves, while commercial banks' foreign exchange holdings also improved.The SBP said Pakistan's reserves had increased by $5 billion since the conflict began in February. Its own holdings rose from $16.568 billion in February to $21.568 billion as of October 30. The central bank said the improved reserve position had helped stabilise the exchange rate and provided exporters with confidence to repatriate their earnings without delay.However, Pakistan continues to face a substantial trade gap. Its trade deficit stood at $14.6 billion in the first four months of FY27, with imports at $26 billion against exports of $11.4 billion. Financial analysts have attributed the stability of the Pakistani rupee and the improvement in foreign exchange availability largely to rising remittances.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $110 million in a week to a record $26.864 billion, according to the State Bank of Pakistan. The rise included a $39 million increase in SBP-held reserves. The SBP said Pakistan's reserves had increased by $5 billion since the conflict began in February.

Article Title: How deep is Pakistan's debt dependence on China? The numbers tell the story
Article Text:
China leads as external debt touches $135 billion

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Pakistan rely more on multilateral institutions for financial aid? Yes, it's safer No, seek private investors 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015, according to a World Bank report cited by Dawn.The figures underline the Islamic country’s growing dependence on foreign borrowing to meet its financial needs.The debt stock comprised $107.07 billion in public and publicly guaranteed loans, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt and $10.45 billion in short-term borrowing.Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.China remained Pakistan’s biggest individual creditor, with outstanding loans of $22.4 billion. The World Bank was next with $19.2 billion, followed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to which Pakistan owed $16.83 billion.The report also highlighted the difference in borrowing costs. Loans from official creditors had an average maturity of 16 years, a four-year grace period and an interest rate of 3.6%. Private credit, in contrast, came at a much steeper average interest rate of 8.6%, with a repayment period of three years and a grace period of just one year.Across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region, debt-service and interest ratios showed improvement.However, the region’s external debt-to-gross national income (GNI) ratio rose from 26.7% to 29.4% in 2025. This was the sharpest annual increase recorded by any region, pointing to a continued build-up of external debt.Pakistan also received some relief through fresh financing and loan extensions during the year. China extended the maturity of $2 billion in loans, while the International Monetary Fund (IMF) disbursed $2.3 billion under its Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility programmes, aimed at supporting the country’s longer-term economic stability.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015. Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.

Article Title: 11 dead, 33 injured in devastating bus-truck collision in eastern Pakistan
Article Text:
.

At least 11 people were killed and 33 others injured after a passenger bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan on Thursday, police and rescue officials said.The accident occurred in Pakpattan district of Punjab province, AP reported, citing hospital official Dr Ahmad Raza. Rescue teams used cranes and other heavy machinery to pull passengers trapped inside the wreckage. The operation lasted nearly three hours, police said.Authorities declared an emergency at the hospital and called in additional doctors and medical personnel to treat the injured, Raza said.Pakistan president Asif Ali Zardari expressed grief over the deaths in a statement, shared on social media, while also extending his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.“Extending his best wishes for the speedy recovery of the injured, he directed the relevant authorities to continue providing all possible support for medical treatment and relief operations,” the statement added.Road accidents are common in Pakistan, where poor road conditions, inadequate enforcement of traffic regulations and unsafe driving practices contribute to frequent collisions. Last month, at least 12 people were killed and around two dozen others injured after a bus collided with a van in the southwestern province of Balochistan, according to AP.
Article Summary: A bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan, police and rescue officials say. Rescue teams used cranes and other heavy machinery to pull passengers trapped inside the wreckage. Pakistan president Asif Ali Zardari expresses grief over the deaths. Road accidents are common in Pakistan, where poor road conditions contribute to frequent collisions.

Article Title: ‘Anti-India’ campaign: Chinese vloggers in Dhaka scale back activities amid increased surveillance
Article Text:
Chinese vloggers filming Dhaka streets. (Image credit: X.com)

Also Read |

Also Read |

(With PTI inputs)

Chinese vloggers accused of defaming India by filming poor neighbourhoods in Dhaka and falsely portraying the footage as scenes from New Delhi have "scaled down" their activities following increased surveillance by local law enforcement agencies, a Bangladeshi police official said.The authorities stepped up monitoring of the Chinese nationals, around 150 in number, after India expressed concern over the alleged use of Bangladeshi territory to tarnish its image.According to Mohammad Khalid Mansur, officer-in-charge of Dhaka’s Uttara West Police Station, intelligence agencies intensified surveillance of the Chinese nationals and began monitoring them closely. This led to a decline in their activities, the newspaper Prothom Alo reported on Thursday.Earlier, Bangladeshi media reports said the Chinese vloggers were active in Dhaka’s Tekpara and Uttara neighbourhoods, livestreaming footage of narrow streets and impoverished localities on Chinese social media platforms. They are accused of misrepresenting these areas as parts of New Delhi and making "disparaging" comments about the residents’ living conditions.The vloggers filmed people’s homes and everyday activities, at times entering residential premises without permission.Residents were unaware of where the footage was being uploaded or how they were being portrayed.The activities are suspected to be part of a coordinated disinformation campaign.“There was no police surveillance of their activities. More than 100 vloggers were making such videos every day. They also paid Bangladeshi citizens to assist them in this work,” Prothom Alo reported.On Tuesday, the ministry of external affairs in New Delhi called for appropriate action against the vloggers for peddling "false narratives" to defame India.Following the controversy, the Chinese nationals were asked to produce their passports and visas and explain why they were engaging in such activities while visiting Bangladesh on tourist visas.Police also instructed them to leave the country upon the expiry of their authorised stay.However, it remains unclear whether a formal investigation has been initiated into their activities or whether any action has been taken over possible violations of visa conditions.Residents, meanwhile, reported that they had not seen any Chinese nationals in Uttara or Tekpara over the past few days."I have been at home for two days due to illness and have not seen any Chinese citizens around," Md Selim, a Tekpara resident, told the newspaper.Rickshaw puller Imamul Islam described a bridge over a canal near Sector 12 in Uttara as a "hideout" for the Chinese vloggers."They would film us throughout the day and night, including our passengers. I haven't seen them around for some time now," he added.
Article Summary: Chinese vloggers accused of defaming India by filming poor neighbourhoods in Dhaka and falsely portraying the footage as scenes from New Delhi. Authorities stepped up monitoring of the Chinese nationals, around 150 in number, after India expressed concern over the alleged use of Bangladeshi territory to tarnish its image.
